reason: Grouping the fibres seems like a useful first step toward building a muscle that can pull on the arm.
expectation: I expect a bundle of muscle fibres, though it may still need connective tissue before it forms a muscle.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels should support the arm, but grouping fibres seems more directly related to the goal.

effect: The fibres formed a bundle, which can now be combined with the connective tissue sheaths.
reaction: The result followed my expectation; the paired poses help connect the bundle to shortening.
reason: Adding sheaths seems like the next step toward an organized muscle.
expectation: I expect a wrapped muscle bundle or a muscle with connective tissue; it may still need attachment to the skeleton.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels also belong in the arm, but I want to finish organizing the fibres first.

effect: The sheaths formed a biceps with tendons, showing how the fibres' pull reaches the bones and why an opposing muscle is needed.
reaction: The link from connective tissue to tendons is clear; the pictured attachment makes me curious about how it will join the arm skeleton.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should help build the arm.
expectation: I expect an arm skeleton supplied with blood vessels, though I am unsure how that will lead to fitting the muscles.

effect: The blood vessels led to an arm assembly with flexor and extensor slots, making the muscle fitting step clear.
reaction: The attachment points clarify how the muscles will join the arm, though the blood vessels' role in creating the assembly was not explained.
reason: The biceps bends the elbow, so it seems suited to the flexor slot.
expectation: I expect the biceps to fill the flexor slot, leaving the extensor slot for the triceps.

alternatives.reason: The triceps should fit the opposing slot, but I chose to attach the biceps first.

effect: The biceps is fitted, leaving the triceps as the remaining offered muscle.
reaction: The fitting was expected and made straightforward progress toward the goal.
reason: The triceps is the only offered combination and should provide the opposing pull.
expectation: I expect the triceps to fill the extensor slot, completing the opposing muscle pair.

effect: The triceps is fitted, and the explanation connects coordinated muscle activity to bending and straightening the elbow.
reaction: The opposing pulls make sense, though the fitting itself was expected.
reason: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues is the only offered combination and should complete more of the arm.
expectation: I expect a more complete arm with the opposing muscles in place, though I am unsure whether this completes the goal.

effect: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues produced a supplied moving arm and completed the goal.
reaction: The completed arm brings the parts together, though the final addition did not explain their roles.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the biceps with tendons was most worthwhile: it connected the fibre bundle to a pull on bone and explained why an opposing muscle is needed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the muscles was straightforward but repetitive; the explanation of their opposing action added more than the fittings themselves.

surprise.text: I did not expect adding blood vessels to create the arm assembly with muscle slots, and their role in that transition was unclear.

arbitrary.text: Adding shoulder and hand tissues felt somewhat arbitrary for completing the opposing-muscle goal because their contribution was not explained.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the moving arm connects to sensing and control. The explanation of how muscle fibres transmit a pull made that prospect interesting.
